question: Greek orange growers and orange juice businesses are complaining about the existence of a ‘cartel’ in Brazil that is controlling orange juice prices worldwide. This creates an uncompetitive business environment, whereby a handful of large companies are unduly amassing huge profits to the detriment of smaller competitors, with Greek and European consumers left at the mercy of unjustified price increases.
Given that the orange juice sector makes a significant contribution to the Greek economy and provides a source of income for thousands of families: 1.
What steps will the Commission take to verify the substance of these complaints, ensure transparent competition and guarantee fair and affordable prices for European consumers?
What are the findings so far from the investigations carried out in the context of the complaints lodged by Greek businesses?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.11.2024) The Commission does not comment on any possible ongoing investigations. It remains open to receive any factual evidence on the matter. The Commission remains at all times committed to assuring an efficient functioning of the Single Market through a thorough competition enforcement.

In case of important harmful violations of the competition rules, through for example illegal agreements or concerted practices between operators, the Commission and National Competition Authorities can carry out antitrust investigations for a possible violation of Article 101 and/ or Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union1,2.
